newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi paper urges Iran to start new era.
newsitem.headline: Saudi paper urges Iran to start new era.

text.p: A newspaper in Saudi Arabia, whose relations with Iran have been tense since the Islamic republic's 1979 revolution, said on Monday it hoped President Mohammad Khatami would usher in a new era of relations with Gulf states.
Al-Riyadh daily said in a commentary the past period seemed not to be suitable "for dialogue and the building of spheres of confidence between the parties.
"Hopes are that the election of President Mohammad Khatami (will lead) to encouraging initiatives for clearer relations particularly with Gulf states."
Saudi newspapers usually reflect the views of the kingdom's government.
Al-Riyadh said Arabs and Iranians were "in the same boat, though differences distanced them from each other".
It said it hoped for better relations with Iran in the near future.

Gulf News, an English-language daily in the United Arab Emirates, said Iran, with a long record of enmity towards the United States, would "find willing listeners to offers of help" if it embarked on adopting fresh policies on both regional and international issues.
The UAE is in dispute with Iran over islands in the Gulf.
Khatami, a Shi'ite Moslem clergyman known for his moderate views, took the oath of office on Monday saying his government would seek dialogue with all nations that respected Iran.
